PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-10-22
40F, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for her yearly wellness visit. She reports occasional wheezing and chest tightness with brisk walking in cold air, easing within a few minutes of rest. She continues to manage episodic distress with regular counseling and coping skills. Over the past several weeks she has noticed intermittent joint aches in the hands and a sun-sensitive facial rash, prompting workup today. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. She works as a teacher. Appetite is good; sleep varies with stress. Lives with her spouse and children. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 74, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 158 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: mild redness over sun-exposed skin of the face.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest today.
Musculoskeletal: mild tenderness at the small joints of the hands, no effusion.
Skin: faint sunburn-like redness over the cheeks.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, CBC within normal limits, ANA negative, urinalysis unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Possible mild intermittent asthma; will trial albuterol. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs before exertion or as needed for wheezing. Inhaler technique reviewed. Spirometry ordered.
2. Rule out lupus; ANA negative. Facial redness fits sun exposure and the joint aches fit repetitive hand use; no further autoimmune testing or rheumatology referral needed. Advised sun protection.
3. Panic disorder, managed with therapy. Continue cognitive behavioral therapy and learned breathing techniques; no medication change requested today.
4. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
5. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography discussed.

Return in 3 months, sooner if the rash spreads or breathing worsens.
